title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Evaluation of bone pain.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman presenting for follow-up of her history of cancer of the right breast. She was treated for the primary malignancy several years ago and has completed all initial treatment protocols. She reports localized discomfort in her skeletal system. She notes that while the primary site shows no evidence of local recurrence, she is experiencing significant discomfort in her back and hips. She denies any new systemic symptoms or fevers.

Medication List
Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. She is in no acute distress but appears to be in mild discomfort when moving. Physical examination reveals localized tenderness over the lumbar spine and hips. No new masses or skin changes are noted on the chest wall.

Assessment
1. Bone metastasis: The patient has developed metastases to bone secondary to her history of right breast carcinoma.
2. History of cancer of the right breast: The primary site remains stable with no evidence of local recurrence.

Plan
We will initiate a regimen of scheduled acetaminophen for bone pain management. We will monitor her comfort levels and schedule a follow-up in four weeks to assess the efficacy of the pain management plan.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/12/2026
explanations: The right female breast cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.3 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
